premise: Adapting a military night-writing code into a tactile reading system for the blind.
hook: A twelve-year-old boy used a discarded military cipher originally meant for soldiers to read in the dark without speaking.
key_facts: Blinded in childhood following an accident in his father's harness shop.
Attended the Royal Institution for Blind Youth in Paris.
Modified Captain Charles Barbier's 'night writing' twelve-dot code into a simpler six-dot cell.
Published his system in 1829, though it was only widely adopted long after his death.

premise: Choosing to test his experimental polio vaccine on himself and his own family.
hook: To prove his vaccine was safe, a medical researcher injected the untested formula directly into the arms of his wife and children.
key_facts: Led a research team at the University of Pittsburgh in the early 1950s.
Utilized a 'killed' virus approach rather than a live-attenuated one.
Announced successful nationwide clinical trial results in April 1955.
Declined to patent the polio vaccine, ensuring it remained accessible globally.

premise: The choice to include Earth sounds and music on a golden record aboard Voyager spacecraft, risking ridicule from orthodox scientists.
hook: What would you say to an alien civilization if you only had one chance to represent all of humanity?
key_facts: Led the committee that placed the Voyager Golden Record aboard the 1977 spacecraft.
Curated sounds of Earth including greetings in 55 languages and music ranging from Bach to Chuck Berry.
Served as professor of astronomy at Cornell University and popularized science through the television series Cosmos.
Co-wrote and presented the landmark PBS series watched by hundreds of millions globally.

premise: Swimming 110 miles from Cuba to Florida at age 64 without a shark cage after decades of failed attempts.
hook: At age 64, after jellyfish stings and asthma attacks stopped her previous tries, she stepped back into shark-infested waters.
key_facts: Attempted the Cuba-to-Florida swim for the first time in 1978 without success.
Resumed long-distance marathon swimming decades later at age 60.
Completed the historic 110-mile crossing from Havana to Key West in 2013.
Spent over 52 hours continuously swimming in open ocean.
